values.note: 26 standard sites book on recreation.gov (or 877-444-6777) up to 4 days before arrival; 15 are first-come, and the rate table runs first-come weeks in mid-May. Weekend reservations 2 nights, holiday weekends 3. A reservation is forfeited if you have not arrived by check-out time the day after your arrival date; walk-up sites cannot be traded for reservations. Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon; self-pay station, no office.

note: Hiawatha NF campground around the south end of 172-acre Monocle Lake, off Lake Shore Drive (Whitefish Bay Scenic Byway) via FR 3699 near Bay Mills, under 2 mi from Point Iroquois Lighthouse; heavily shaded sites in mixed hardwoods. Day-use picnic area with a swimming beach, and the Monocle Lake Trail with an accessible boardwalk. Concession-run. Repaving is scheduled for autumn 2026 and spring 2027, during the seasonal closure (FS alert, October 2026). --Claude
summary: FS page (updated 2026-09-14) + recreation.gov: $24 (confirmed, 2027 unchanged), half-price Senior/Access (new), no hookups (confirmed), 42 sites (new) with 26 reservable / 15 first-come so fcfs some_sites (new), max rig 50 -> 80 ft (catalog, 2 sites; most 30-50), pull-throughs (confirmed), vault toilets + pressurized water (confirmed), season June 12 - Sept 13 (new, FS), 2-night weekend / 3-night holiday minimums, 14-night limit, booking closes 4 days before arrival (new). The FS page's 'Site Closed' banner is the seasonal closure; the repaving alert says the work is scheduled during it, so no status was written. No Hiawatha alert closes Lake Shore Drive or FR 3699. Ownership: federal land run by a concessionaire (FS page: 'Concessionaire can be reached at (906) 767-1111'; '$7.00 per additional vehicle per day applies in all concessionaire campgrounds'), although recreation.gov marks it not commercially managed.
Season conflict: FS 'Seasons of Use June 12 - September 13' vs recreation.gov rate seasons starting May 14 (first-come) and May 22 (peak) in 2026; the FS dates were written with both in season.note.

Waterfront re-audit lead: entry is 'not waterfront', but recreation.gov says 'The campground surrounds the south end of 172-acre Monocle Lake ... providing scenic lake and forest views from anywhere in the campground' and the FS page speaks of being 'camped along the shores of a lovely inland lake'.
